title: Sounding natural
goal: React like a local, use tag questions and emphasis particles, make echo words, ask people to repeat, slow down or explain, get round words you don't know, and mix in English the way Tamils do.
intro:
You can know all the grammar and still sound like a textbook. What makes spoken Tamil sound alive is the small stuff: the reactions (**சான்ஸே இல்ல!** 'no way!', **அடப்பாவி!**), the tags that pull the listener in (நல்லா இருக்கு**ல்ல**? 'it's nice, isn't it?', நீ வருவ**தானே**? 'you're coming, right?'), the little particles of emphasis (இப்போ**வே** 'right now', ஒரு காபி**யாவது** 'at least a coffee'), and **echo words** like **காபி கீபி** 'coffee or something'.

This unit also gives you the survival kit for real conversations — asking people to repeat or slow down, asking what a word means, filling a gap while you search for a word — and a look at how Tamils mix English into almost every sentence.

grammar.title: Tag questions: -ல்ல?, தானே?, சரியா?
grammar.body:
Tamil tags go at the very end and invite the listener to agree.

**-ல்ல?** (from இல்ல 'not'), glued to the verb, is the everyday 'isn't it? didn't we?': நல்லா இருக்கு**ல்ல**? 'it's nice, isn't it?'; after a consonant it's written -ல: போன வருஷம் வந்தோம்**ல**? 'we came last year, didn't we?'. The full form **இல்லையா?** is more insistent: நீ சொன்ன, இல்லையா? 'you said so, didn't you?'.

**தானே?** 'right? surely?' — you expect a yes: நீ நாளைக்கு வருவ**தானே**? 'you're coming tomorrow, right?'; இது உன் பை**தானே**? 'this is your bag, isn't it?'. Said flat, without the question tone, தானே means 'after all': அவன் சின்னப் பையன்**தானே** 'he's only a kid, after all'.

**சரியா?** 'OK?' after a request or a plan: ஏழு மணிக்கு வா, சரியா? Politer: **சரிங்களா?**

**-ஆ** on any single word makes a quick echo question — the most common reaction of all: நாளைக்கா? 'tomorrow?', நீயா? 'you?', ஐநூறா? 'five hundred?!'.

**Answers:** ஆமா 'yes', **ஆமாமா** 'yes, totally', **பின்ன!** 'of course!', **இல்லையே** 'no, not at all' (the -ஏ makes it a firm, slightly surprised no).

examples.en: The film was good, wasn't it?
We came here last week, didn't we?
He's just a kid after all — let it go.

grammar.title: More emphasis: -ஏ, -ஆவது, கூட, -ஓ and ஒரே
grammar.body:
Unit 20 showed you **-தான்**, **-உம்** and **-ஏ**. Here are the rest of the little words that make Tamil sound alive. Each one sticks to the word it stresses.

**-ஏ 'right, very, itself'** on time and place words: இப்போ → **இப்போவே** 'right now', அங்க → **அங்கேயே** 'right there', நாளைக்கே 'tomorrow itself'. On a negative it means 'at all': நம்பவே முடியல 'I just can't believe it'; doubled verb, even stronger: புரியவே புரியாது 'I just don't get it at all'.

**-ஆவது 'at least'**: ஒரு காபி**யாவது** குடிங்க 'at least have a coffee', ஒரு தடவை**யாவது** 'at least once'.

**கூட 'even'** after the word: ஒரு ரூபா **கூட** இல்ல 'not even one rupee', அவனுக்கு **கூட** தெரியும் 'even he knows'.

**-ஓ 'I wonder / some…'**: மழை வருமோ? 'I wonder if it'll rain', என்னமோ 'something or other', எங்கேயோ 'somewhere'. Doubled, it means 'whether … or': வருவாரோ இல்லையோ 'whether he comes or not'.

**ஒரே 'so much, nothing but'** before a noun: ஒரே கூட்டம் 'such a crowd', ஒரே சத்தம் 'nothing but noise'.

And to swear something's true: **சத்தியமா**: சத்தியமா நான் சொல்லல 'I swear I didn't say it'.

examples.en: Leave right now, or you'll be late.
Come to Madurai at least once.
I don't even have ten rupees on me.
I don't know whether he'll come or not.

grammar.title: Echo words and doubled words
grammar.body:
**Echo words** add 'and stuff, or anything' to a noun. Repeat the word, swapping its first consonant + vowel for **கி** (or **கீ** if the vowel is long): காபி → காபி **கீ**பி 'coffee or something'; புத்தகம் → புத்தகம் **கி**த்தகம் 'books and stuff'; பணம் → பணம் **கி**ணம்; கோபம் → கோபம் **கீ**பம். If the word starts with a vowel, the vowel becomes கி: இட்லி → இட்லி கிட்லி.

The echo makes things casual and friendly: காபி கீபி சாப்பிடுறியா? 'fancy a coffee or something?'. It also plays down a worry: கோபம் கீபம் இல்லையே? 'you're not angry or anything, are you?'. Keep it for friends and family — it's too casual for an office email.

**Doubled words** show repetition, spreading out or intensity: மெல்ல மெல்ல 'little by little', சின்னச் சின்ன 'all the little', வேற வேற 'all sorts of different', தப்பு தப்பா 'all wrong, full of mistakes'. Sounds are doubled and followed by -ன்னு: சொட்டு சொட்டுன்னு 'drip-drip', பளபளன்னு 'gleaming'. (You also know the doubled infinitive from unit 38: பாக்கப் பாக்க.)

examples.en: Would you like a coffee or something?
You're not angry or anything, are you?

examples.native: பணம் கிணம் எதுவும் வேணாம், சும்மா வா.
examples.roman: paṇam kiṇam eduvum vēṇām, summā vā.
examples.en: You don't need money or anything, just come.
Little by little, Tamil has started to make sense.
Don't get stressed about every little thing.

dialogue.title: Madurai Tamil
dialogue.setting: Tom, who has been learning Tamil for a year, is at a café in Chennai with his friend Priya and her cousin Sathya, who is visiting from Madurai.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: டாம், உன் தமிழ் வேற லெவல் ஆயிடுச்சு!
lines.roman: Ṭām, un tamiḻ vēra leval āyiḍucchu!
lines.en: Tom, your Tamil has gone to the next level!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: சீரியஸா? சத்தியமா நான் இன்னும் தப்பு தப்பாதான் பேசுறேன்.
lines.roman: sīriyasā? sattiyamā nān innum tappu tappādān pēsurēn.
lines.en: Seriously? Honestly, I still make mistakes all the time.

lines.speaker: Sathya
lines.en: So Tom, how're you doing? (Madurai style)

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: Hang on… 'irukkeegala'? What does that mean?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: அது மதுரை பாஷை. “இருக்கீங்களா”ன்னு அர்த்தம். சத்யா மதுரைக்காரன்தானே!
lines.roman: adu Madurai bāshai. “irukkīngaḷā”nnu arttam. Sattyā Maduraikkārandānē!
lines.en: That's Madurai lingo. It means 'irukkeengala'. Sathya's from Madurai, after all!

lines.speaker: Sathya
lines.native: ஆமா, எங்க ஊர் பேச்சே தனி. உங்களுக்கு சென்னை தமிழ்தான் பழக்கம், இல்லையா?
lines.roman: āmā, enga ūr pēcchē tani. ungaḷukku Chennai tamiḻdān paḻakkam, illaiyā?
lines.en: Yes, the way we talk back home is something else. You're used to Chennai Tamil, aren't you?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: ஆமா. ஆனா ஆக்சுவலி, சென்னையில எல்லாரும் பாதி இங்கிலீஷ்தான் பேசுறாங்க.
lines.roman: āmā. ānā āksuvali, Chennaiyila ellārum pādi inglīshdān pēsurānga.
lines.en: Yes. But actually, in Chennai everyone speaks half in English.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: பின்ன? “ஜஸ்ட் வெயிட் பண்ணு, டூ மினிட்ஸ்ல வர்றேன்”னு தான் சொல்லுவோம்!
lines.roman: pinna? “jasṭ veyiṭ paṇṇu, ṭū minitsla varrēn”nu dān solluvōm!
lines.en: Of course! We say things like 'just wait, I'll be there in two minutes'!

lines.speaker: Sathya
lines.native: அடப்பாவி, நீங்க ரெண்டு பேரும் என்னை நக்கல் பண்றீங்களா?
lines.roman: aḍappāvi, nīnga reṇḍu pērum ennai nakkal paṇrīngaḷā?
lines.en: Hey! Are you two making fun of me?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: இல்லையே! சரி, காபி கீபி ஏதாவது சாப்பிடலாமா?
lines.roman: illaiyē! sari, kāpi kībi ēdāvadu sāppiḍalāmā?
lines.en: Not at all! OK, shall we have a coffee or something?

lines.speaker: Sathya
lines.en: Now you're talking! Tom, you're brilliant!

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: சரி சரி, இப்போவே ஆர்டர் பண்ணுங்க. இங்க டக்குன்னு ஒரே கூட்டம் ஆயிடும்.
lines.roman: sari sari, ippōvē ārḍar paṇṇunga. inga ṭakkunnu orē kūṭṭam āyiḍum.
lines.en: OK, OK, order right now. This place gets packed in no time.

culture:
**Tanglish** — Tamil mixed with English — is completely normal, especially in Chennai and among younger people and professionals: English nouns and adverbs (actually, basically, seriously, just, office, meeting) slot into Tamil grammar, and English verbs take **பண்ணு**: வெயிட் பண்ணு, கால் பண்ணு, ட்ரை பண்ணு. Older people and Tamil purists may prefer 'pure' Tamil, and many people switch to more Tamil with elders.

Spoken Tamil varies a lot by region (**வட்டார வழக்கு**). **Chennai** street Tamil (மெட்ராஸ் பாஷை) is fast and full of slang; **Kongu** Tamil around Coimbatore is famously polite, with -ங்க on almost everything; **Madurai** Tamil has forms like **இருக்கீக** for இருக்கீங்க; **Tirunelveli** speakers say **ஏலே** 'hey'; and Sri Lankan Tamil sounds different again. Films mix them all, so you'll learn to recognise them.

Listen for the fillers that keep a conversation flowing: **ம்ம்** and **ஆமா ஆமா** (I'm listening), **வந்து…** and **அது…** (um…), **சரி** (OK, so…), and **அப்புறம்?** (and then? / so, what's new?). And don't be shy about asking: Tamils are usually delighted when a foreigner speaks even a little Tamil, and happy to slow down — கொஞ்சம் மெதுவா பேசுங்க works wonders.

tip.title: Reactions
tip.body:
- Surprise: **ஓ!**, **அப்படியா?**, **நிஜமாவா?**, **சீரியஸா?**
- Disbelief: **சான்ஸே இல்ல!**, **அடப்பாவி!** (mock outrage — friends only).
- Praise: **சூப்பர்!**, **தெறி!**, **வேற லெவல்!**, **கலக்கிட்ட!**
- Swearing it's true: **சத்தியமா**.

sentences.en: Oh, really? I had no idea at all.
You rascal — you got married without telling me?
I swear I didn't tell anyone!
This biryani is killer!
You were brilliant in the match yesterday!
Biryani for a hundred rupees? No way!
Are you serious, or just joking?

sentences.native: இந்த ஏரியா ஃபுல்லா மாறிடுச்சு, வேற லெவல்!
sentences.roman: inda ēriyā fullā māriḍucchu, vēra leval!
sentences.en: This area has completely changed — it's on another level!

tip.title: Tags: -ல்ல? · தானே? · சரியா?
tip.body:
- **-ல்ல?** glued to the verb = 'isn't it? didn't we?': நல்லா இருக்கு**ல்ல**? வந்தோம்**ல**?
- **தானே?** = 'right? surely?' (you expect yes): நீ வருவ**தானே**?
- **சரியா?** after a request = 'OK?'.
- Answer: ஆமா, **பின்ன!** 'of course!', **இல்லையே** 'not at all'.

sentences.en: This coffee's great, isn't it?
You saw that film, didn't you?
You've eaten, haven't you?
Don't forget to call tomorrow, OK?
She's our friend after all — we can invite her.
This is your bag, right?
Hmm… OK, we'll see.
Can I come too? Of course, definitely come!

tip.title: Right now, at least, even: -ஏ · -ஆவது · கூட · -ஓ
tip.body:
- **-ஏ** 'right, very': இப்போ**வே** 'right now', அங்கே**யே** 'right there'.
- **-ஆவது** 'at least': ஒரு காபி**யாவது**.
- **கூட** 'even': ஒரு மணி நேரம் **கூட** 'not even an hour'.
- **-ஓ** 'I wonder': மழை வருமோ?  **ஒரே** 'so much': ஒரே கூட்டம்.

sentences.en: Tell me right now, or you'll forget.
At least have a coffee before you go.

sentences.native: நேத்து ஒரு மணி நேரம் கூட தூங்கல.
sentences.roman: nēttu oru maṇi nēram kūḍa tūngala.
sentences.en: I didn't sleep even an hour last night.
The sky's dark — I wonder if it'll rain?

sentences.native: என்னமோ தெரியல, இன்னைக்கு ஒரே தூக்கமா வருது.
sentences.roman: ennamō teriyala, innaikku orē tūkkamā varudu.
sentences.en: Dunno why, I'm so sleepy today.
The beach is packed!
Come over to my place at least once.
OK, and then? What did he say?

sentences.native: டக்குன்னு ஒரு முடிவு எடு, எல்லாரும் வெயிட் பண்றாங்க.
sentences.roman: ṭakkunnu oru muḍivu eḍu, ellārum veyiṭ paṇrānga.
sentences.en: Decide quickly — everyone's waiting.
You're treating us? Now you're talking!

tip.title: Echo words: காபி கீபி
tip.body:
- Repeat the noun, swapping its first syllable for **கி** (short vowel) or **கீ** (long vowel): பணம் → பணம் **கி**ணம், காபி → காபி **கீ**பி.
- It means 'X or something, X and stuff' — casual and friendly.
- Doubled words: மெல்ல மெல்ல 'little by little', தப்பு தப்பா 'full of mistakes'.

sentences.en: Want some tea or something?
Don't mess about — I'm asking seriously.

sentences.native: புக் கிக் எதுவும் வேணாம், சும்மா வா.
sentences.roman: buk kik eduvum vēṇām, summā vā.
sentences.en: You don't need books or anything, just come.
If he asks for money or whatever, don't give it.

sentences.native: சாப்பாடு கீப்பாடு எதுவும் வேணாம், வயிறு ஃபுல்.
sentences.roman: sāppāḍu kīppāḍu eduvum vēṇām, vayiru ful.
sentences.en: No food or anything for me, I'm full.

sentences.native: வண்டி கிண்டி எதுவும் இல்ல, நடந்துதான் வந்தேன்.
sentences.roman: vaṇḍi kiṇḍi eduvum illa, naḍandudān vandēn.
sentences.en: I haven't got a bike or anything — I walked.
There's always a bit of sarcasm in the way he talks.
Even if you make mistakes, it doesn't matter — just talk!
His name won't come to me right now.

tip.title: Keeping up
tip.body:
- 'Didn't get it': **புரியல**. 'Again, please': **திரும்ப ஒரு தடவை சொல்லுங்க**.
- 'Slower': **கொஞ்சம் மெதுவா பேசுங்க** ('you're fast': ரொம்ப **ஸ்பீடா** பேசுறீங்க).
- 'What does X mean?': X-ன்னா என்ன **அர்த்தம்**?
- 'How do you say…?': … தமிழ்ல **எப்படிச் சொல்லுவீங்க**?

sentences.native: நீங்க ரொம்ப ஸ்பீடா பேசுறீங்க, கொஞ்சம் மெதுவா.
sentences.roman: nīnga romba spīḍā pēsurīnga, konjam meduvā.
sentences.en: You're talking really fast — a bit slower, please.
What does 'kalaaykkiradhu' mean?
How do I pronounce this word?
Is my pronunciation all right?
Sorry to interrupt — I have a question.
Could you explain in a bit more detail?
What's the English word for that?
Oh, now I get it!

Basically, he doesn't like the job, that's all.

sentences.roman: sīriyasā solrēn, nī oru ḍākṭaraip pāru.
sentences.en: I'm serious — go and see a doctor.
Just five minutes, I'll be there.

sentences.native: சென்னையில எல்லாரும் தமிழும் இங்கிலீஷும் கலந்துதான் பேசுவாங்க.
sentences.roman: Chennaiyila ellārum tamiḻum inglīshum kalandudān pēsuvānga.
sentences.en: In Chennai everyone speaks a mix of Tamil and English.
The Coimbatore way of talking is very polite.

sentences.native: ஒவ்வொரு ஊருக்கும் ஒரு வட்டார வழக்கு இருக்கு.
sentences.roman: ovvoru ūrukkum oru vaṭṭāra vaḻakku irukku.
sentences.en: Every town has its own dialect.
I just can't understand Tirunelveli Tamil at all!
